clue.text: He works wonders in magazine article here in France

parts.note: ici is the French word for here
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wonder-worker turns up in a French magazine feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror or wizard is someone who performs marvels and seemingly impossible feats.

clue.text: One ruined by gin a lepidopterist?

explanation.surface: A butterfly collector has been brought low by drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin is nicknamed 'mother's ruin' in Britain. The question mark flags a pun: a lepidopterist studies moths, so is a 'moth-er'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin's slang name 'mother's ruin' makes a parent its victim, and a student of moths could playfully be called a moth-person.

clue.text: Something to gladden a man's heart from this bush telegraph

definitions.text: Something to gladden a man's heart from this bush telegraph

parts.words: Something to gladden a man's heart from this bush telegraph
parts.note: the plant that yields wine, which the Psalm says makes glad the heart of man, and also the informal rumour network called the bush telegraph

explanation.definitionFit: The vine bearing wine grapes is the bush, and an informal word-of-mouth rumour network is the bush telegraph's other name.

clue.text: Sacred vessel found by girl under church

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl's name sits beneath the church abbreviation

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A holy cup is discovered by a young woman beneath a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A consecrated cup holding communion wine is the sacred vessel of the Eucharist.

clue.text: Skill without energy in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for skill goes around the word for energy

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Someone talks skilfully but lacks any vigour in their delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense of 'outside', so energy is surrounded rather than removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon or slang peculiar to a group is a particular way of talking.

clue.text: Failed to catch what none on Ko-Ko's list would be

definitions.text: what none on Ko-Ko's list would be

explanation.surface: Someone fails to catch the people on a list from comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, Ko-Ko sings of his 'little list' of social nuisances who 'never would be missed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a ball or a train is a failure to catch, and the Mikado song says nobody listed would be mourned in absence.

clue.text: In which certain questions are asked in court

definitions.text: In which certain questions are asked in court

parts.note: taken as written
quest in its old sense is an inquiry or questioning

explanation.surface: Describing a court hearing at which particular questions are put.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a coroner's hearing while its first word and a sense of 'questions' build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner's official judicial investigation into a death takes evidence and asks questions in a court.

clue.text: Stick notes on it

explanation.surface: An instruction to fix some memos somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking pole or rod is a stick, and the five lines of musical notation carry notes.

clue.text: Living here, a winter fuel gatherer

definitions.text: Living here, a winter fuel gatherer

parts.words: Living here, a winter fuel gatherer
parts.note: the home of the poor man in the carol Good King Wenceslas, seen gathering winter fuel, whose home the king asks about

explanation.walkthrough: The carol Good King Wenceslas asks of a peasant 'gath'ring winter fuel': 'Where and what his dwelling?'
explanation.definitionFit: A house or abode is a place where someone lives.

clue.text: Royalty incorporated in the fourth estate

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for the fourth estate

parts.note: the press is traditionally called the fourth estate

explanation.surface: A member of royalty is made part of the newspaper world.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's daughter is a member of a royal family.

clue.text: Horatio highly honoured and lionized here

definitions.text: Horatio highly honoured and lionized here

parts.words: Horatio highly honoured and lionized here
parts.note: the London place where Horatio Nelson stands high on his column, surrounded by bronze lion statues

explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column in central London is guarded by four bronze lions, so 'lionized' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: London's square commemorating Nelson's naval victory holds his tall column and Landseer's lions.

clue.text: Gray supporter in a change of site

indicators.note: in puts the limb inside the rearranged letters
a change of means the letters of the next word are altered

parts.note: taken as written for anagram
a leg supports a body or table

explanation.surface: A grey-haired backer is involved in relocating to a new place.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray looks like a colour but is Thomas Gray, author of Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray was a poet best known for a mournful lament, so he is a writer of elegies.

clue.text: Wherewithal to end fuel disruption

indicators.note: disruption means the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Funds are needed to stop disruption to fuel supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption' rearranges END FUEL; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The needful' is a colloquial term for money, the means or resources required.

clue.text: Excellent Russian brew for a Yorkshire terrier?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as the letter I
red was a common label for a Soviet Russian
ale is a brewed beer

explanation.surface: A first-rate Russian drink is offered for a dog from Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this breed is a terrier from Yorkshire, not the Yorkshire Terrier breed itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed named after a Yorkshire valley is a large terrier native to that county.

clue.text: One of Kubla Khan's prophets of war

definitions.text: One of Kubla Khan's prophets of war

parts.words: One of Kubla Khan's prophets of war
parts.note: Coleridge's poem has Kubla hear voices of forebears prophesying war

explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Kubla Khan: 'Kubla heard from far / Ancestral voices prophesying war!'
explanation.definitionFit: The voices in the poem are ancestral, so each speaker is a forebear of the Khan.

clue.text: Doctor preserved by Athenian misanthrope

annotationWithheld.why: Doctor preserved by Athenian misanthrope (5): MO inside TIN needs 'preserved' to give TIN (tinned) and also to act as the container indicator; one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Coal stratum perhaps plays a role in coastal defence

definitions.text: plays a role in coastal defence
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the ship that does this job; the definition describes what the vessel does

parts.note: a coal mine, coal standing for the pit that yields it
a stratum is a layer of rock

explanation.surface: A seam of coal is said to help defend the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks coal as an example of what a mine yields. The definition describes the ship's function.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that lays explosive charges at sea protects harbours and shores from enemy ships.

clue.text: Strong supporter of amendment of law in the beginning

indicators.note: in places the altered letters inside the word for beginning

parts.note: start means the beginning

indicators.note: an amendment alters the letters of the following word

parts.note: taken as written for anagram

explanation.surface: A firm backer supports changing a law from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amendment of' rearranges LAW to LWA, which goes 'in' START.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal, steadfast backer of a cause or party is a sturdy partisan.

clue.text: Very continental head of silver hair

parts.note: très is French for very

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A head of silver hair seen on a European.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock or long strand of hair is a curl.

clue.text: Editors reshaped by a body-builder possibly

indicators.note: reshaped means the letters of editors are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: Journalists' editors are remodelled by a muscleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshaped' rearranges EDITORS; 'possibly' hedges the definition, since such a drug builds muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic drugs are used to build muscle mass, so one may build bodies.

clue.text: Roger's window charmed open by the song of Keats's nightingale

definitions.text: window charmed open by the song of Keats's nightingale

explanation.surface: A window opened by the bird's song in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Casement was an Irish nationalist executed in 1916. Keats's Ode to a Nightingale speaks of 'magic casements, opening on the foam'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger's surname belongs to the Irish rebel, and a hinged window opening outward is the frame in Keats's ode.

clue.text: Press goddess

explanation.surface: Squeeze a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Minerva Press was a London publisher of popular sentimental novels around 1800.
explanation.definitionFit: A publishing house famous for Gothic romances took its name, and the Roman deity of wisdom bears it too.

clue.text: Unemotional, when 501 sale items are put up

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the letters run upwards

parts.note: D is 500 and I is 1 in Roman numerals
lots are items sold at auction

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm while hundreds of auction pieces are offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are put up' turns DILOTS upwards; 'put up' also suggests offered for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmatic, impassive person shows no feeling, being dull and calm.

clue.text: Those carrying out minor operations on the dance-floor?

definitions.text: Those carrying out minor operations on the dance-floor?

parts.words: Those carrying out minor operations on the dance-floor?
parts.note: people who lance boils, read alongside a nineteenth-century set dance of that name

explanation.definitionFit: Lancing is a small surgical procedure, and a quadrille for couples bears the same name.

clue.text: Inert sort of chemical

indicators.note: sort here is a verb meaning arrange, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of chemical that does not react.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges INERT, though it reads as 'kind of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a chemical compound used in gunpowder.

clue.text: One sort of shirt an athlete may wear

parts.note: single means one
a T-shirt is a kind of shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: A kind of top that a runner might put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest is the garment a runner competes in.

clue.text: Woman is upset by a riddle

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: taken as written
Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: A woman is troubled by a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IS to SI, set above EVE. A riddle is also a coarse sieve, not just a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle in its older sense is a coarse mesh strainer for soil or gravel.

clue.text: Did Halley perhaps rely on a star room?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the following words might be put another way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the comet man depended on an observatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RELY ON A STAR ROOM. Edmond Halley was the second holder of this post.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Halley held the royal post of chief British astronomer from 1720.

clue.text: Go outside the limit, it's fashionable

indicators.note: outside puts the word for go around the word for limit

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
an end is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: Exceeding the bounds is all the rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a noun here, an attempt, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in vogue follows the latest style or craze.

clue.text: Made good when given different partners

explanation.surface: Things were fixed once couples were swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Mending something restores it, and being matched afresh with new partners is being paired again.
